payload.selection_rationale: One proposal (practice) was handed in. I selected its core against what the survey and spikes measured. Reality already holds every input: ScanStore has every file with charged sizes, and GetPath is proven exact for 400-char, trailing-dot, trailing-space and lone-surrogate names (spike unusual-name-long-path-roundtrip, go). Nothing ranks or displays files. So the slice is one read-only query in Core, one virtualized ListBox copied from the UnreadableList pattern, and two or three scalars on the existing --report path. That is the simplest thing that works. The proposal's own over_engineering_flag was treated as a real signal. The popular answer (Hugefile Finder: thresholds, streaming, sortable columns, delete, CSV) is rejected wholesale, and open-in-Explorer, copy, delete and a live list are left for later slices. Ranking by ChargedOnDisk with both sizes shown is kept. It follows the project's counting constraint, is a one-line key swap to reverse, and is recorded as a default and as an open question. Bounded PriorityQueue, a fixed top 100, and computing once in ShowOutcome after the scan has stopped are kept. Nothing in the tree contradicts them and every one is cheap to reverse. Three additions come from checking the proposal against the criterion that "anywhere under the scanned folder" must be true. (1) The caption also states unreadable folders, because 663 folders were unreadable in the C:\ spike and their files can never appear. (2) `largestFilesMs` goes on the report so the untested UI-thread cost at millions of entries is a measured number rather than "no visible stall". (3) One architecture rule is declared where the proposal declared none. The counting rules are the project's no-corners area, and the next analysis slices will inherit this folder. The path column wraps instead of trimming, so a 400-character location is never hidden.

components.name: LargestFiles (Scan Analysis)
components.responsibility: New static class with `Top(ScanStore store, int count)`, the first code in the architecture's Scan Analysis block. One pass over entries 0..Count-1. It keeps an entry only if Kind == EntryKind.File and (ChargedSize > 0 or ChargedOnDisk > 0), which drops later hardlink names, links and empty files (all charge 0). Survivors go into a PriorityQueue bounded at `count`, min-heap on the tuple (ChargedOnDisk, ChargedSize, -index), using EnqueueDequeue to replace the root. The heap is drained and reversed so the output is largest first, and each row gets Path = store.GetPath(index). It reads only charged values and never touches the filesystem. Memory is O(count). The returned rows are plain values and strings, so no reference into the store survives.
components.lives_at: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Analysis/LargestFiles.cs (new; the record type LargestFile(int Index, string Path, long ChargedSize, long ChargedOnDisk) sits in the same folder). The folder is fixed by this design because the architecture rule below is scoped to it.
components.key_interactions: Reads the public ScanStore accessors Count, Kind, ChargedSize, ChargedOnDisk and GetPath. Called once by MainWindow.ShowOutcome. Tested directly by LargestFilesTests. Governed by the architecture rule.

components.name: ScanStore and ScanResult (unchanged)
components.responsibility: Data source. It holds one entry per file and folder as index-addressed columns, rebuilds any entry's full path, and states the counting rule (ScanStore.cs:81). This slice makes no change to the store, the scanner or the counting rules. The scanner's writers stay internal.
components.key_interactions: Read-only for this slice. ScanResult supplies Store, Status, the file total and the Unreadable list that the panel caption uses.

components.name: Largest-files panel
components.responsibility: A section in the outcome panel of MainWindow, above the unreadable-folders list. It has a header 'Largest files, by space on disk', a caption, and a virtualized ListBox (Recycling mode, fixed MaxHeight so it scrolls inside the panel). Each row shows on-disk size, logical size, and the full path in a wrapping TextBlock, so a long location is never clipped. Sizes use the byte formatter ShowOutcome already uses. A small App-side row type carries the pre-formatted strings, so Core stays free of formatting. The caption reads 'Top {shown} of {files} files', plus 'in the part read before the scan stopped' when Status is not Completed, plus 'files in {n} unreadable folders are not included' when Unreadable is non-empty. Zero rows shows 'No files found'. `const int LargestFilesShown = 100` lives in the App. ShowOutcome calls Top synchronously, times the call, and sets ItemsSource. The scan-start handler clears ItemsSource and hides the section. A scan that produced no store leaves the section hidden.
components.lives_at: src/ App project: MainWindow.xaml and MainWindow.xaml.cs (ShowOutcome around MainWindow.xaml.cs:266-312; the pattern to copy is UnreadableList at MainWindow.xaml:41 and MainWindow.xaml.cs:297-305)
components.key_interactions: Consumes LargestFiles.Top and ScanResult. Feeds the report scalars from the bound collection, not from a recomputation.

components.name: Window report fields
components.responsibility: Three additive scalars in the schema-1 `--report <file>` output: largestFilesShown (int, rows actually bound), largestFileOnDisk (long or null, first row's on-disk bytes) and largestFilesMs (the measured Top duration). No paths and no listing, per Q-016. The report must be written after ShowOutcome has filled the list, and the build has to confirm the existing writer's ordering. If eng/read-window.ps1 rejects unknown keys it is updated in the same commit. The schema stays 1.
components.lives_at: The App's existing --report writer under src/ (find it by grep for the schema-1 writer), and eng/read-window.ps1
components.key_interactions: Written by the App, read by eng/read-window.ps1 and asserted by the window case.

components.name: LargestFilesTests
components.responsibility: xUnit Facts in the existing Core.Tests project. Each builds a real tree in %TEMP%, runs Scanner.Scan, then calls LargestFiles.Top. They exercise every material shape in `cases` that Core can see. Link tests fail loudly if creation fails (Q-001, Developer Mode is on); they are never skipped. Sparse and hardlink helpers are reused from the existing counting-rule tests.
components.lives_at: Core.Tests project, new LargestFilesTests.cs beside TraversalTests.cs
components.key_interactions: Runs through eng/dotnet.ps1, which Q-003 permits to bootstrap SDK 10 into the gitignored .dotnet/.

components.name: Window case for the list
components.responsibility: One case in the existing window-test path. It launches the published exe on a planted tree with `--report`, and asserts largestFilesShown, largestFileOnDisk and largestFilesMs and that no planted file name appears in the report. Facts the report cannot see (row text, the caption, a lone-surrogate path rendering, the panel layout beside a filled unreadable list) are checked by driving the published exe once at validate.
components.lives_at: tests/window/ (WindowCases.ps1 and its data), through eng/read-window.ps1
components.key_interactions: Uses the existing FsaWindowHook and StallRig conventions. It adds no App test project and no UIA.

components.name: Analysis reads only the store's charged values (rule)
components.responsibility: The one architecture rule this design declares. It is mirrored in ArchitectureRulesTests and .taad/fitness.yaml, and eng/rules-parity.ps1 must stay green. One plant row proves it fires. Q-010 applies: the rule is appended to the existing rules file on trunk and does not create it.
components.lives_at: .taad/fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests in Core.Tests, eng/rules-harness plant-row data
components.key_interactions: Scoped to src/FsAnalyser.Core/Analysis/**, which this slice creates. Later analysis slices (largest folders, by extension) inherit it.

contracts.name: LargestFiles.Top
contracts.auth_model: none (in-process, read-only over an in-memory store)
contracts.error_cases: A null store throws ArgumentNullException. count < 0 throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. count == 0 returns an empty list. Fewer qualifying files than count returns all of them, with no padding. It does not throw for odd names, because GetPath is proven for them. It must be called only on a store the scanner has stopped writing (Completed or Cancelled). Calling it on a live scan is not part of this slice's contract.
contracts.notes: `static IReadOnlyList<LargestFile> Top(ScanStore store, int count)`, `readonly record struct LargestFile(int Index, string Path, long ChargedSize, long ChargedOnDisk)`. Order: ChargedOnDisk descending, then ChargedSize descending, then store index ascending. The key includes the index, so it is a total order and no two entries tie. Index order follows scan order, which is multithreaded, so tests must not assert an order among files with identical sizes. A hardlinked file is listed under whichever name the scan charged, which can differ between two scans of the same tree.

contracts.name: Largest-files panel
contracts.error_cases: No store means the section stays hidden. Zero qualifying files shows 'No files found'. A new scan starting clears and hides the section before any progress shows. A cancelled scan shows a list built from what was read, and says so.
contracts.notes: ACCEPTANCE the later gates read (the slice has no formal criteria, so this design states them). (1) After a finished scan the person sees up to 100 rows, ordered by on-disk size then logical size, both shown, and the header names the basis. (2) Rows cover files at any depth under the chosen root and never include a folder. (3) Each row shows the file's full path, never clipped. (4) A hardlinked file appears once, links and empty files do not appear. (5) A partial scan and unreadable folders are stated in the caption, so the list never claims to be the whole tree when it is not. (6) A new scan never shows the previous scan's list. Out of scope: column sorting, open-in-Explorer, copy, delete, threshold, user-set count, live update during a scan.

contracts.name: --report schema-1 additions
contracts.error_cases: When no scan has finished, largestFilesShown is 0, largestFileOnDisk is null and largestFilesMs is null.
contracts.notes: Additive scalars only: largestFilesShown, largestFileOnDisk, largestFilesMs. No paths and no listing, which honours Q-016. The schema stays 1 unless eng/read-window.ps1 cannot tolerate new keys, in which case the keys are added there in the same commit instead of bumping the schema.

key_decisions.decision: Rank by ChargedOnDisk (space actually taken), tie-break on ChargedSize, and show both sizes on every row. The header names the basis. This is a default the slice text left open, recorded so nobody has to read it out of the code.
key_decisions.rationale: The list exists to find what is using the disk, and the project's counting constraint says both sizes matter because of compressed, sparse and online-only files. Ranking by logical size puts OneDrive online-only files (large logical size, 0 on disk) at the top, and deleting them frees nothing locally. Both sizes are shown, so no information is lost. Changing the basis swaps the heap key and the header text. It is also an open question for the person.

key_decisions.decision: Only EntryKind.File entries with ChargedSize > 0 or ChargedOnDisk > 0 qualify, and every size is read through ChargedSize / ChargedOnDisk.
key_decisions.rationale: ScanStore.cs:81 and docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:19 require anything that ranks sizes to use charged values. Later hardlink names and links charge 0, so the filter drops them without knowing the flag layout. A duplicate's raw Size can be stale, and this filter never reads it. A file with logical size but 0 on disk (sparse, online-only) still qualifies via the OR, so it is shown when the list is not full.

key_decisions.decision: Show a fixed top 100. The constant lives in the App and Core takes the count as a parameter.
key_decisions.rationale: The slice text leaves the count open. 100 matches what the cited Largest Files Finder shows, covers the cleanup candidates on a real drive, and needs no paging. A threshold or user-set count is out of scope.

key_decisions.decision: One O(n log N) pass with a bounded PriorityQueue rather than collecting and sorting all files.
key_decisions.rationale: The C:\ spike scan held 3,570,999 files, and U-001 measured 699 MiB of a 1 GiB budget. A full sort would add a roughly 14 MB index array plus sort time. The heap is O(N) memory and allocates nothing per entry.

key_decisions.decision: Compute synchronously in ShowOutcome once per Completed or Cancelled scan. Clear at scan start. Record the duration in the report as largestFilesMs.
key_decisions.rationale: The scanner has stopped writing by then, so there is no reader/writer question, and the report can be written after the list is filled. The UI-thread cost at millions of entries has not been measured. The report scalar makes it a number validate can read against the real C:\ scan (4.4M entries). If it stalls visibly, only the Top call moves to Task.Run and the report write still follows the fill. A live list during the scan is not needed by any of the four criteria.

key_decisions.decision: The location is the full path from ScanStore.GetPath in one wrapping column. There is no open-in-Explorer, copy, or name/folder split.
key_decisions.rationale: GetPath is the only record-to-path function and is proven exact for long, dot-ending, space-ending and lone-surrogate names. Splitting name from folder would need an accessor nobody has confirmed, or Path.GetDirectoryName over odd names nobody has tested. Wrapping instead of trimming keeps the whole location readable, which is what 'showing where each one is' asks for. Open-in-Explorer is its own Desktop UI item and becomes a follow-up.

key_decisions.decision: The caption states when the list is not the whole tree: a cancelled scan, and unreadable folders (with a count).
key_decisions.rationale: The criterion says 'anywhere under the scanned folder'. The C:\ spike showed 663 unreadable folders, and any file inside one can never appear. Saying so is cheaper than a list that silently claims completeness. It was added on top of the proposal, which covered only the cancelled case.

key_decisions.decision: Declare one architecture rule: files in src/FsAnalyser.Core/Analysis/** must not call the store's raw Size/OnDisk accessors and must not use file-system APIs. The build confirms the exact accessor shape in ScanStore.cs and adjusts the regex in the same commit. A plant row must prove it fires.
key_decisions.rationale: The proposal declared none. The counting rules are the project's one no-corners area, and the rule was previously prose at ScanStore.cs:81. Later analysis slices will be written in this folder, and one raw-size read there would double-count hardlinks or report stale sizes while every test on this slice stayed green. The cost is one rule mirrored in ArchitectureRulesTests and .taad/fitness.yaml under eng/rules-parity.ps1, plus one plant row.

key_decisions.decision: The report gains three scalars (count, first row's on-disk bytes, compute milliseconds) and never a path.
key_decisions.rationale: Q-016 says the report holds totals and never a listing. With no App test project, the report is the only way validate can prove the list was filled and correctly topped on a planted tree. Every scalar has a reader (the window case), so none is written for nobody.

architecture_rules.name: the analysis code reads sizes only as the store charged them, and only from the store
architecture_rules.because: The store's raw Size and OnDisk skip the counting rules: a hardlink's later names, links, and a duplicate's stale size all charge or read wrongly. A ranking built on them lists one file twice or shows a wrong size, and the tests for that one function would still pass. Asking the disk again bypasses the store's measured values and costs minutes on a multi-million-entry drive. Only ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk, read from the store, carry the rules. The build confirms the raw accessor shape (call or indexer) in ScanStore.cs and fixes the first pattern in the same commit if it differs. A plant row must show the rule fires, because a glob that matches nothing can never fail.

cases.behaviour: rank the largest files under the scanned root
cases.shape: files at the top level and six folders down, where a folder's total is larger than any single file
cases.why: Recursive coverage is the criterion. A top-level-only walk, or a missing Kind == File check, would leave out the deep file or list the folder.

cases.shape: more files than count (105 files, count 100), with several sharing the same size at the cut
cases.why: The EnqueueDequeue replace-the-root path only runs past capacity. The result must be exactly the 100 largest, descending, with no duplicates. The tie-break on index must keep the output a total order.

cases.behaviour: list a tree that has nothing to rank
cases.shape: an empty folder, or a folder holding only zero-length files
cases.why: Empty files charge 0 and are filtered, so the heap stays empty. The panel must say 'No files found' rather than show an empty box or throw on a first-row read for the report.

cases.behaviour: list a file that has more than one name
cases.shape: a 3 MiB file with a second hardlink in another folder
cases.why: Later names charge 0. A raw Size read would list the file twice, which the counting constraint forbids. Exactly one row must appear, with non-zero charged sizes.

cases.shape: a symbolic link to a file, a symbolic link to a folder, and a junction to a folder
cases.why: Links are not followed and charge 0. The target file must be listed once and no row may come from a link. Link creation failing fails the test (Q-001), it is not skipped.

cases.behaviour: rank by space on disk with both sizes shown
cases.shape: a sparse file of 64 MiB logical and about 0 on disk beside a dense 1 MiB file
cases.why: This is the ranking-basis decision. The dense file must rank above the sparse one. The sparse file must still appear when the list is not full (the OR in the filter), with correct values in both columns. It also models the online-only shape.

cases.shape: a path over 260 characters, a name ending in a dot, a name ending in a space, and a name with an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate
cases.why: The spike proved GetPath on scratch copies. This locks it in the tree. Each returned path must equal the created string exactly, with no truncation, no U+FFFD and no stripped trailing dot or space.

cases.behaviour: list from a scan that was stopped
cases.shape: a Cancelled scan holding only what was read before the stop
cases.why: The list must come from the partial store without throwing and the caption must say so. It also settles the must-verify invariant that Scanner.Scan has joined its writers before it returns, so no entry is read half-written.

cases.shape: a second scan begins (or fails before any entry) after a list has been shown
cases.why: A stale list shown as the current scan's is the past reported as the present. The scan-start handler must clear and hide it, and a failed scan must leave the section hidden.

cases.behaviour: state what the list does not cover
cases.shape: the biggest file sits inside a folder the scan could not read
cases.why: That file can never be in the list. The caption must name the unreadable-folder count so the list does not claim the whole tree. This is checked at validate by driving the published exe.

cases.behaviour: fit the list into the outcome panel
cases.shape: 100 rows, one with an unpaired-surrogate path, with the unreadable-folders list also filled
cases.why: A ListBox in an unbounded StackPanel loses virtualization and its scrollbar and can push the unreadable list off screen. WPF drawing a lone surrogate has not been shown not to throw. Neither is visible in Core tests, so validate drives the exe.

cases.shape: the report written after a finished scan of a planted tree
cases.why: With no App test project, the report is the only machine-readable proof for criterion 4. The scalars must come from the bound collection and be present when the report is written. The report must contain no planted file name (Q-016). eng/read-window.ps1 must tolerate the new keys.

cases.shape: a store near 4-5 million entries (the real C:\ scan had 4,417,469)
cases.why: The synchronous UI-thread cost is unmeasured. largestFilesMs read from a real large scan decides whether the Top call moves to Task.Run.

cases.behaviour: rank a file whose size the scanner had to probe
cases.shape: open and growing, probe failed, or an online-only OneDrive placeholder
cases.why: The list reads only ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk and never branches on how the store obtained them. The scanner side is already covered by the spike open-growing-file-stale-directory-size (256 MiB logical, 257-264 MiB on disk) and OnDiskSizeTests. A real OneDrive placeholder cannot be built in %TEMP%, and the sparse-file case models the same (logical > 0, on-disk 0) shape. The next slice can disagree with this.

proposals.note: The only proposal handed in. Its core is taken whole: the bounded-heap query, ranking by on-disk with both sizes shown, top 100, compute once after the scan, and the trimmed UI. Added on top: unreadable-folder and partial-scan caption, largestFilesMs on the report, wrapped path column, one architecture rule, and a window case. The crossdomain and expert designers were not run.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, no composition to check. Nothing in this design has yet survived a disagreement, and the reviewer should argue with it first. The seams I checked against what the survey measured:

1. Counting rule. The filter and the ranking key both read only ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk, which is what ScanStore.cs:81 requires. The design and the new rule agree on that.
2. Ownership. Top returns plain values and strings and keeps no reference into the store. Clearing the list at scan start therefore cannot affect the scan's memory, which U-001 measured at 699 MiB of 1 GiB.
3. One error contract. Top throws only for caller mistakes (null store, negative count). The App passes a constant and calls it only after Scan returns, so a failed or absent scan hides the section and never reaches Top. Report scalars are 0 or null in that case.
4. Ordering assumption not checked by anyone: the report must be written after ShowOutcome fills the list. The proposal asserted this, and neither it nor this design read the existing report writer. If the report is written from an earlier completion hook, the fix is to fill the list first, which is small and does not change a boundary.
5. Every thing produced has a reader. Top is called by ShowOutcome, the rows by the ListBox, the report scalars by the window case, and the caption inputs come from ScanResult. There is no settle without a reader.
6. Q-016 and the report. The additions are scalars only and never paths, so they are consistent with the recorded storage line. Nothing is written to disk.

What I changed at the seams:
- The proposal declared no rules. I declared one rule with two patterns, because a raw-size read in this folder is a counting defect that would pass every test on this slice. This obliges the build to mirror it in ArchitectureRulesTests and .taad/fitness.yaml and keep eng/rules-parity.ps1 green, plus one plant row. If the parity harness cannot express must_not_match rows, that is an obligation to raise, not a reason to drop the rule silently.
- I added the unreadable/partial caption and `largestFilesMs`, so the criterion 'anywhere under the scanned folder' is not silently false and the UI-thread risk is a number.

Nothing project-scope was chosen. PriorityQueue is BCL and the panel is a WPF ListBox, so stack_chosen is empty. Nothing here has been built or run on the project's own toolchain. The machine has SDK 8 and 9 only, and every spike ran on copies of Core with a side-installed SDK. The build must go through eng/dotnet.ps1, which Q-003 permits. The exact folder names for tests and the report writer, and the shape of the raw Size accessor, are inferred from the survey and are for the build to confirm.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Relational query execution: ORDER BY ... LIMIT N
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Top-N heapsort. A column scan feeds a bounded heap instead of a full sort, as in PostgreSQL's top-N heapsort plan. The ScanStore is a struct-of-arrays columnar table with the index as row id, so the query is ORDER BY charged_on_disk DESC LIMIT 100 WHERE kind = File AND charged > 0.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The pattern fits directly. It avoids fully sorting about 3.5M rows against a tight memory budget, and a comparator that is a total order (the index breaks ties) makes the output deterministic. It is a standard top-K rather than a deep import, so the design does not lean on the analogy beyond the algorithm.

invariants.precondition: The ranking key does not change during the pass (no concurrent writer).
invariants.evidence: Holds for Completed scans. For Cancelled scans, nobody has confirmed that Scanner.Scan has joined its background writers before it returns. The build reads Scanner.cs first, and the Cancelled-scan case covers it.

invariants.precondition: The comparator is a total order, so the output is deterministic for a given store.
invariants.evidence: The key (ChargedOnDisk, ChargedSize, index) is unique per entry because the index is unique.

invariants.precondition: N is much smaller than the row count, so the heap beats a sort.
invariants.evidence: N = 100 against 3,570,999 files in the spike's C:\ scan.

invariants.precondition: The filter is applied before ranking and uses the same measure as the key.
invariants.evidence: Both read charged values only. Raw Size and OnDisk are never read, and the architecture rule enforces it.

decidable_disagreements.question: By the time a Cancelled ScanResult reaches ShowOutcome, has Scanner.Scan already joined its background writers, so the store is stable to read?
decidable_disagreements.positions: Nobody contested it, because only one designer was run. The proposal assumes yes, and the design's 'compute once after the scan has stopped' depends on it. If no, the contract must change: either the scanner quiesces before returning (a change in the counting-rule code, at a higher review tier) or Top must be given a snapshot. Reading Scanner.cs and running the Cancelled-scan case settles it.

open_questions: Should the list rank by space actually taken on disk (the design's default, with both sizes shown) or by logical size? A person looking for 'the biggest files' may expect logical size, and it would put OneDrive online-only files near the top. The slice text did not settle it. Changing it swaps the heap key and the header text.

On C:\, pagefile.sys (20 GiB in the spike), hiberfil.sys (about 12.5 GiB) and swapfile.sys will lead the list. Should they be shown unlabelled (the design's default, since the spike measured them as correct), labelled as system files, or left out?
taste_disagreements: No one contested any of these: one proposal, no rival. Ranking basis (on-disk versus logical) is also an open question above.
A fixed top 100 in an App constant versus a threshold or a person-set count.
Full path in one wrapping column versus separate name and folder columns, which would need a name accessor nobody has confirmed.
The list as a section inside the outcome panel above the unreadable list versus its own expander or tab.
Computing on the UI thread inside ShowOutcome versus Task.Run from the start. The report's largestFilesMs is meant to settle this with a number.
LargestFiles under a new Core/Analysis folder, with the rule scoped to it, versus a flat Core folder.
One architecture rule with two patterns, versus none (the proposal's choice) or two separate rules.

prior_art.pattern: Top-100 largest files for a chosen drive or folder. Each row shows file name, full folder path, size and modified date.
A Largest Files report whose purpose is space recovery. It shows where each space-consuming file is.
Top-x largest files on a drive (default 10) with a configurable count.
The bloated version: a size threshold, streaming results, sortable columns, delete and Recycle Bin actions, CSV export and open-directory. Everything past the list itself is out of scope here.
A Path | Size | Type | Relative table of the biggest files after a recursive scan.
Disk analysers keep separate 'Size' and 'Allocated' columns, because logical size misleads for compressed, sparse and cloud-placeholder files.
Bounded top-K with PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority>.EnqueueDequeue, which gives O(n log k) work and O(k) memory.
A ListBox placed in a StackPanel is measured with infinite height, so it loses UI virtualization and its scrollbar. The fix is a bounded height or a star Grid row.
